rule.in_words: A header that carries an account root (acc, acct, accnt, subacc) enters the AR-y-194 value backstop ONLY when every other word of it stands in its allowed place: a word BEFORE the root must be an ACCOUNT_MODIFIERS word, a word AFTER the root must be an ACCOUNT_TAIL_WORDS word (or another root). The attribute-word blocklist (ACCOUNT_ATTRIBUTE_WORDS, _has_account_root, _has_attribute_word) is removed, because nothing else used it. Repair (b) of r19.2 (a digit run of 8 or more is an identifier only when no value in its column carries a number separator) is kept. The whole-cell exclusions ACCOUNT_HEADER_EXCLUDED and the header rule are unchanged apart from the two words below.
rule.consequence_for_unlisted_words: An unknown word keeps a header OUT of the backstop (CTO round-21 ruling). A header whose other words are not all in the allowed places is not read as an account column by the backstop, whatever its values. 'Acct Ref Ext' is the worked case: 'ext' is in neither list, so the header is not admitted and two identifier-like values are NOT turned back. This is the allowlist's price and it is pinned by test_an_account_root_header_with_an_unlisted_word_is_not_read_as_an_account_column.
rule.why_by_position: The ruling reads 'every other word is an identifier-tail word, with alias added to the tails and primary to the modifiers'. Read as a word set over tails and modifiers together, 'Acct Custodian' is admitted, because custodian is an ACCOUNT_MODIFIERS word, and its values SCHWAB01 and FIDELITY1 are turned back, against a named control. The header rule's own grammar places a modifier before the account word and a tail after it, so the test uses that position (surprise row W67-S2).
rule.why_by_position_detail: _root_header_admitted(text): words = _header_words(text); the first root index r; before = words[:r] must all be in ACCOUNT_MODIFIERS; after = words[r+1:] must all be in ACCOUNT_TAIL_WORDS or ACCOUNT_ROOTS. 'Acct' alone is admitted (both lists empty).

word_sets_as_built.header_rule_effect_of_added_words: 'Account Alias' and 'Primary Account' (and 'Primary Acct', 'Primary Acct No') now match the header-word rule through _is_account_header, because primary is a modifier and alias a tail word. ACCOUNT_HEADER_EXCLUDED is unchanged.
